why: What the house collects, from whom, for what, and who else receives it: read from the code (WORKLIST P1.6). The Privacy Policy, the App Store privacy answers, Play's data safety form (store/forms/) and the app's privacy manifest (app.json ios.privacyManifests) are written from it. thePrivacyInventoryIsWhole fails if a shipped package, a table holding a member's id or a user agent, an outside host the code names, or a required-reason API a package declares is missing here, and if a store form was prepared from another version of this file.

email.purpose: The account: signing in, a forgotten password, confirming the address, deleting the account, and the house's notices about the account.

names.what: The member's username and the name they show (which may be their real name).
names.purpose: Who the member is to other members: on their writing, in salons, on their page.

member-id.what: The member's account number (a random id the house gives each account) and their username as a handle.
member-id.purpose: Tying the member's writing, purchases and notices to their account; RevenueCat is told the account number so a purchase reaches the right account.

portrait.what: The portrait a member chooses for their page, from their photos or camera.
portrait.purpose: Shown on the member's page and beside their writing.

writing.what: What a member writes and keeps: logs, reviews, critiques, Dispatch posts and essays, comments, stacks and lists, their shelf of physical copies, private notes, drafts, their bio, and what they import from a file they choose.
writing.purpose: The member's own record of films, kept for as long as the account exists and read by the members they choose.

salon-messages.what: Messages and reactions a member sends in a salon, and the salons they found or join.

actions.what: What a member does to others' writing and to members: endorsements, votes, saves, certifications, follows, blocks, and the reports they file.
actions.purpose: Shown to the members it concerns (an endorsement, a follow), keeping a blocked member away, and moderation.

purchases.what: A member's rank purchases: which rank, from which store, when it began and ends.
purchases.purpose: Granting the rank paid for, and restoring it on another phone.

push-token.what: The address Apple or Google gives the phone for the app's notifications, with the phone's platform; on the website, the browser's notification address and its keys.
push-token.purpose: Sending the member the notifications they keep on.

install-id.what: A random number expo-updates gives each install of the app, sent with the platform and the app's version when the app asks for an update.

notices.what: The notifications the house sends a member, and who caused each.
notices.purpose: The member's notices, read in the app.

searches.what: The words a member searches for films and people with.
searches.purpose: Finding the film or person; passed by the house's own server to TMDB, so TMDB never sees who asked.

sign-in-records.what: The IP address and browser or app name (user agent) of each sign-in and session, kept by Supabase Auth.
sign-in-records.purpose: The account's security: sessions, and seeing a sign-in that was not the member's.

moderation.what: What the house's moderators decide about a member: warnings, sanctions in a salon, actions taken, and a piece withheld from the Lobby.
moderation.purpose: Keeping the house's rules, and a member's right to know why.
moderation.whyNoForm: Made by the house about a member, not collected from them; named in the Privacy Policy.

crashes.what: What the app was doing when it failed: the error, the code's path to it, the phone's model and system, the app's version and the member's rank, never their id, name or email (Sentry's sendDefaultPii is off). The website sends the same, and times 10% of visits.

play.type: App info and performance: Crash logs

website-errors.what: An error the website met while a member was signed in: the error, the page, the browser's user agent, and the member's id.
website-errors.purpose: Finding and fixing what fails on the website.
website-errors.whyNoForm: The website's alone; the store forms are the app's.

website-visits.what: Which pages a signed-in member opens on the website.
website-visits.purpose: Knowing which of the website's pages are read.
website-visits.whyNoForm: The website's alone; the store forms are the app's.

website-analytics.what: PostHog's record of a visit to the website, only if the website's PostHog key is set.
website-analytics.purpose: Knowing how the website is used.
website-analytics.when: VITE_POSTHOG_KEY is set in a Vercel project that serves the website; none does (the owner, 2026-11-06), so it is never made
website-analytics.whyNoForm: The website's alone; the store forms are the app's.

support-letters.what: A letter a member writes to the front desk from their own mail app: their email, what they write, and what the app puts in it (the app's version, the phone's model, the member's account number).

supabase.who: Supabase: the house's own server, database, sign-in and file store

auth-mail.who: Resend (smtp.resend.com), the mail server set in Supabase Auth's SMTP settings, which sends the confirm, reset and deletion-code letters from team@thereelhousesociety.com

tmdb.who: TMDB, the film database: the house's server asks it for films; the app and website load its posters and pictures directly

youtube.who: YouTube: a trailer the member opens plays from YouTube's privacy-enhanced address; trailer pictures load from YouTube

revenuecat.who: RevenueCat: reads the store's receipt and tells the house which rank a member holds

app-store.who: Apple's App Store: takes the payment, through the phone's own purchase sheet

google-play.who: Google Play: takes the payment, through the phone's own purchase sheet

expo-push.who: Expo's push service, which hands the house's notifications to Apple and Google

expo-updates.who: Expo's update service: the app's updates

front-desk-mail.who: The front desk's mail: Cloudflare forwards support@ to the house's Gmail; replies go out through Resend

house-website.who: The house's website, served by Vercel; the app opens its pages (help, the rules, privacy)

posthog.who: PostHog: the website's visit analytics, only if its key is set; no Vercel project sets it (the owner, 2026-11-06), so it receives nothing

rss2json.who: rss2json: the website reads a film news feed through it; nothing of the member is sent

links.why: Addresses the app hands to the phone's browser or store when the member taps them; the app itself sends nothing there.

notReached.dummy.supabase.co: supabase.ts's stand-in when a build has no address; every production build has one (eas.json), and the release guard refuses a build without it.

@expo-google-fonts/courier-prime.why: Font files built into the app.

@expo-google-fonts/inter.why: Font files built into the app.

@expo-google-fonts/rye.why: Font files built into the app.

@expo-google-fonts/special-elite.why: Font files built into the app.

@expo-google-fonts/spectral.why: Font files built into the app.

@expo/vector-icons.why: Icon glyphs built into the app.

@hookform/resolvers.why: Checks a form's fields on the phone.

@react-native-community/netinfo.why: Reads the phone's connection; on an iPhone it asks the house's sign-in server whether it can be reached (src/lib/reachability.ts), never Google's address it asks by default.

@sentry/react-native.why: Crash and performance reports, without the member's id, name or email.

@supabase/supabase-js.why: Everything the member keeps and reads in the house.

@tanstack/react-query.why: Holds what was read on the phone.

@tanstack/react-query-persist-client.why: Keeps what was read on the phone between launches.

base64-arraybuffer.why: Turns a picture into bytes on the phone before its upload (sent by supabase-js).

expo-application.why: Reads the app's own build number on the phone.

expo-clipboard.why: Copies text the member asks to copy.

expo-crypto.why: Makes random ids and hashes on the phone.

expo-dev-client.why: A development tool; the release guard proves its launcher is not in a store build.

expo-device.why: Reads the phone's kind on the phone (a real phone or a simulator, its memory class); sent nowhere.

expo-document-picker.why: Opens the file a member chooses to import; it is read on the phone and what it holds is kept as their writing.

expo-file-system.why: Reads and writes files on the phone.

expo-font.why: Loads the fonts built into the app.

expo-image.why: Loads posters, portraits and trailer pictures from their addresses.

expo-image-manipulator.why: Resizes a chosen portrait on the phone.

expo-image-picker.why: Lets the member choose a portrait from their photos or camera; only the one chosen is uploaded (by supabase-js).

expo-local-authentication.why: Face ID or a fingerprint, answered by the phone; nothing of it reaches the app.

expo-notifications.why: Asks for the phone's notification address and shows notifications.

expo-secure-store.why: Keeps the sign-in in the phone's keychain.

expo-sharing.why: Opens the phone's share sheet for what the member shares.

expo-store-review.why: Asks the phone to show its own rating prompt.

expo-updates.why: Asks for the app's updates, with the install's random number.

expo-web-browser.why: Opens a page in the phone's browser sheet.

jszip.why: Opens an import file on the phone.

react-dom.why: Needed by packages that draw with it; the app draws none on the phone.

react-native-mmkv.why: Keeps settings and saved reads on the phone, encrypted.

react-native-purchases.why: Purchases, with the member's account number.

react-native-view-shot.why: Makes a picture of a card the member shares, on the phone.

react-native-webview.why: Plays a trailer the member opens.

react-native-worklets.why: Runs motion off the main thread.

memberColumnsWithoutKey.why: Columns that hold a member's id with no foreign key to say so (WORKLIST P3.6), and the id columns named like them that hold something else.

requiredReasonApis.why: Apple's required-reason API categories the app or its packages use, with the reasons they give. Each package's own manifest is in node_modules, or (Sentry, RevenueCat, SDWebImage) in the pod CocoaPods fetches; expo-updates, expo-sharing and react-native-mmkv use one and ship no manifest. The app's manifest (app.json ios.privacyManifests) declares all of them, as a statically linked pod's manifest is not always carried into the app.
